headline: Highest risk is medium: plano can ingest and forward argo-workflows outputs, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of shared storage or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts/parameters and expose REST/gRPC APIs, while Plano accepts OpenAI-compatible chat inputs and has an out-of-process dataplane. That creates a plausible bridge where Argo-produced content is fed into Plano as trusted instructions. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are copied into Plano prompts without provenance filtering
IF a shared API or queue passes Argo-generated text to Plano as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Argo outputs before passing them onward
Strip tool directives from Argo-generated text before Plano ingests it
Require a human review step for any prompt assembled from Argo artifacts
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents behind separate queues with schema validation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, and Plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, same OAuth principal, or automatic file upload, so leakage is possible only through operator-mediated transfer or logging. That keeps the blast radius limited and the pathway non-default.
conditions: IF operators place Argo artifacts into Plano logs or prompts
IF both agents are pointed at the same external storage path
mitigations: Keep Argo artifacts out of Plano prompt text
Disable verbose logging for any shared workflow run
Use separate storage buckets or directories for each agent
Review Plano logs for accidental artifact capture

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has API-based workflow control and Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus config.yaml, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem write, git mutation, or multiple-instance coordination. The overlap is mainly read/ingest and API-facing, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty stays low because the missing write surfaces are informative.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable resource
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one shared config or state file
mitigations: Assign separate output directories for each agent
Lock any shared config file before edits
Avoid concurrent writes to the same API resource
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level mutexes for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce artifacts and parameters that Plano may consume as chat-completion input. If Plano treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from workflow generation into downstream routing or responses. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF Plano uses Argo-produced text as the sole source for downstream decisions
IF no verification or schema check is inserted between Argo and Plano
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Argo output and Plano input
Require citations or structured fields before Plano acts
Compare Argo outputs against a second source for critical decisions
Flag low-confidence Argo outputs for manual review

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic data classes, with no PHI, EU PII, or residency claims. That means no specific compliance breach is evidenced; the only plausible issue is a mismatch in retention or logging if operators route sensitive data through both. Because the other agent is not cited for a unique residency constraint, the risk remains low.
conditions: IF sensitive regulated data is routed through both agents
IF an operator relies on undocumented retention or residency behavior
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair without a policy review
Document retention settings for both systems
Minimize logs for any workflow carrying sensitive inputs
requires-engineering: add data-class-based routing controls
